claim: ph505 mitotic mutant clones were generated using the Flp/FRT system in eye-antennal imaginal discs.
source: ph505 mitotic mutant clones were generated using the Flp/FRT system, allowing for specific tumor growth within eye-antennal imaginal discs (from here on referred to as ph505-tumor).
evidence: The manuscript directly states the experimental method used to generate mutant clones.

claim: Mutant clones were fluorescently labeled with GFP using the MARCM system.
source: Mutant clones were fluorescently labeled with GFP, by using the mosaic analysis with a repressible cell marker (MARCM) system (Wu and Luo, 2006).
evidence: The manuscript describes the labeling method with citation to the MARCM system.

claim: Reduced expression of Ph in ph505 mutant clones was observed compared to FRT19A control tissues.
source: Reduced expression of Ph in the mutant clones compared to tissues carrying FRT19A (neutral) mitotic clones was observed (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: The manuscript states the observation and references supporting figures.

claim: Only a small number of larvae carrying ph505-tumors reached adulthood.
source: Only a small number of larvae carrying ph505-tumors reached adulthood (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The manuscript directly states this observation with reference to supporting data.

claim: ph505-tumors display disrupted cell polarity.
source: The majority of tumors arising in these epithelial tissues display disrupted cell polarity (Martinez et al., 2009), which was confirmed using the cell adhesion marker Armadillo (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D–E).
evidence: The manuscript states this observation with citation and reference to supporting figures.

claim: Ectopic expression of Matrix metalloprotease 1 (MMP1) was observed in ph505-tumors.
source: Additionally, we observed ectopic expression of Matrix metalloprotease 1 (MMP1) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F–G), which is required for matrix degradation and the invasive potential of tumor cells (Christofi and Apidianakis, 2013; Uhlirova and Bohmann, 2006).
evidence: The manuscript describes the observation with citations and reference to supporting figures.

claim: Neoplastic growth of ph505 mutant clones can be rescued by wild-type ph co-expression.
source: Here we show for the first time that neoplastic growth of ph505 mutant clones in eye-antennal imaginal discs can be rescued by wild-type ph (via UAS-ph) co-expression.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this as a novel finding.

claim: Tissues with restored Ph levels harbored smaller clones compared to tissues containing ph505 clones.
source: The resulting tissues with restored Ph levels harbored smaller clones compared to the tissues containing ph505 clones (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H–I).
evidence: The manuscript states this observation with reference to supporting figures.

claim: In tissues with ph505 clones, 46% of the disc was composed of tumor cells.
source: We found that in tissues with ph505 clones 46% of the disc was composed of tumor cells, while in the rescue experiment this ratio was reduced to only 7% (Figure 1—figure supplement 1K–N).
evidence: The manuscript provides quantitative data with reference to supporting figures.

claim: In the rescue experiment with UAS-ph, the tumor volume was reduced to 7% of the disc.
source: We found that in tissues with ph505 clones 46% of the disc was composed of tumor cells, while in the rescue experiment this ratio was reduced to only 7% (Figure 1—figure supplement 1K–N).
evidence: The manuscript provides quantitative data with reference to supporting figures.

claim: The eclosion rate of ph505 pupae was less than 20%.
source: Consistent with these observations, a reduced number of larvae carrying ph505-tumors reached adulthood (eclosion rate <20%).
evidence: The manuscript provides quantitative data on eclosion rate.

claim: The eclosion rate of ph505, UAS-ph pupae was 97%.
source: In contrast the eclosion rate of ph505, UAS-ph pupae (97%) was similar to control flies (99%) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1J).
evidence: The manuscript provides quantitative data with reference to supporting figures.

claim: The tumorigenic phenotype of ph505 tissues is primarily due to the loss of ph.
source: Overall, these results show that the tumorigenic phenotype of ph505 tissues is primarily due to the loss of ph since it can be rescued by the expression of the wild-type protein.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion based on rescue experiments.

claim: Tumors with impaired ph do not accumulate genetic instabilities.
source: We had shown previously that tumors with impaired ph do not accumulate genetic instabilities, even when cultivated for prolonged time in adult hosts (Sievers et al., 2014).
evidence: The manuscript cites previous work to support this claim.

claim: The neoplastic behavior of ph505-tumors can be solely restricted to the loss of the silencer ph and the ensuing deregulation of the transcriptional state.
source: Hence, the observed neoplastic behavior can be solely restricted to the loss of the silencer ph and the ensuing deregulation of the transcriptional state described below.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion based on the lack of genetic instability and rescue experiments.

claim: RNA sequencing was performed on FACS-sorted ph505 tumor cells and surrounding wild-type cells.
source: To better understand the molecular consequences of polyhomeotic loss-of-function in vivo, we analyzed the transcriptome of ph505-tumor cells by RNA sequencing (RNA-seq). We used fluorescence activated cell sorting (FACS) of dissociated eye-antennal imaginal discs to separate GFP-labeled tumor cells from surrounding unlabeled and non-mutant cells (Martinez et al., 2009; Dutta et al., 2013; Harzer et al., 2013).
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental approach with citations.

claim: 1337 genes were differentially expressed in ph505-tumor cells compared to neighboring non-mutant cells.
source: We identified 1337 differentially expressed genes (Benjamini adjusted p-value, padj. <0.01), with 275 genes being upregulated in ph505-tumor cells (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: The manuscript provides quantitative data from RNA-seq analysis with reference to figures.

claim: 275 genes were upregulated in ph505-tumor cells.
source: We identified 1337 differentially expressed genes (Benjamini adjusted p-value, padj. <0.01), with 275 genes being upregulated in ph505-tumor cells (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: The manuscript provides quantitative data from RNA-seq analysis with reference to figures.

claim: 1062 genes were downregulated in ph505-tumor cells.
source: We identified 1337 differentially expressed genes (Benjamini adjusted p-value, padj. <0.01), with 275 genes being upregulated in ph505-tumor cells (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: The manuscript states 1337 total differentially expressed genes with 275 upregulated, implying 1062 downregulated (1337-275=1062).

claim: Neurogenesis-related genes were mainly downregulated in ph505-tumor cells.
source: Furthermore, gene set enrichment analysis revealed that neurogenesis-related genes were mainly downregulated in ph505-tumor cells, while genes regulating transcription were upregulated (Figure 1B).
evidence: The manuscript states this finding from gene set enrichment analysis with reference to a figure.

claim: Genes regulating transcription were upregulated in ph505-tumor cells.
source: Furthermore, gene set enrichment analysis revealed that neurogenesis-related genes were mainly downregulated in ph505-tumor cells, while genes regulating transcription were upregulated (Figure 1B).
evidence: The manuscript states this finding from gene set enrichment analysis with reference to a figure.

claim: Genes involved in tissue development were deregulated in ph505-tumor cells.
source: Moreover, we observed deregulation of genes involved in tissue development (e.g., GO-terms for genital disc development, imaginal disc development) and enrichment for TFs among the upregulated genes (GO-term sequence-specific DNA binding transcription factor activity) (Figure 1B, Figure 1—source data 2).
evidence: The manuscript states this observation with reference to GO-term analysis and figures.

claim: There was enrichment for transcription factors among the upregulated genes in ph505-tumor cells.
source: Moreover, we observed deregulation of genes involved in tissue development (e.g., GO-terms for genital disc development, imaginal disc development) and enrichment for TFs among the upregulated genes (GO-term sequence-specific DNA binding transcription factor activity) (Figure 1B, Figure 1—source data 2).
evidence: The manuscript states this observation with reference to GO-term analysis and figures.

claim: The global modulation of transcription output is in agreement with PcG proteins constituting a global regulatory system.
source: The observed global modulation of transcription output is in agreement with PcG proteins constituting a global regulatory system (Simon and Kingston, 2009).
evidence: The manuscript states this interpretation with citation to support the claim.

claim: ph505-tumor cells clustered close to samples from early embryonic developmental stages in hierarchical clustering analysis.
source: Strikingly, hierarchical clustering of 83 transcriptome samples showed that ph505-tumor cells clustered close to samples from early embryonic developmental stages (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The manuscript states this finding from clustering analysis with reference to figures.

claim: Control samples (neighboring unlabeled cells) clustered with wild-type eye-antennal imaginal disc transcriptomes.
source: As expected, our RNA-seq control samples (neighboring unlabeled cells) clustered with wild-type eye-antennal imaginal disc transcriptomes.
evidence: The manuscript states this expected result from clustering analysis.

claim: The clustering of ph505-tumor cells with early embryos may reflect the re-establishment of an earlier developmental program as a consequence of a reprogrammed epigenomic state.
source: This result might reflect the re-establishment of an earlier developmental program in ph505-tumors as a consequence of a reprogrammed epigenomic state.
evidence: The manuscript proposes this interpretation of the clustering results.

claim: Clustering with embryos is not a general feature shared by all tumors.
source: Additionally, this is not a general feature shared by all tumors, as depicted by other tumor types (i.e. brat [Jüschke et al., 2013] and RasV12/scrib- tumors [Atkins et al., 2016]) not clustering with embryos.
evidence: The manuscript states this observation with citations to other tumor types.

claim: ELAV expression is downregulated in ph505-tumor cells.
source: We confirmed the downregulation of neurogenesis-related markers at the protein level for ELAV (Embryonic Lethal Abnormal Vision), which is normally expressed in the differentiated neuronal cells that make up the eye imaginal disc (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–B)
evidence: The manuscript confirms downregulation at protein level with reference to figures.

claim: Eya (Eyes absent) expression is downregulated in ph505-tumor cells.
source: We confirmed the downregulation of neurogenesis-related markers at the protein level for ELAV (Embryonic Lethal Abnormal Vision), which is normally expressed in the differentiated neuronal cells that make up the eye imaginal disc (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–B) and for Eya (Eyes absent, Figure 1—figure supplement 3C–D).
evidence: The manuscript confirms downregulation at protein level with reference to figures.

claim: Neoplastic Drosophila epithelial cells reverse their developmental commitments and switch to primitive cell states.
source: This supports previous findings that suggested that neoplastic Drosophila epithelial cells reverse their developmental commitments and switch to primitive cell states (Khan et al., 2013).
evidence: The manuscript cites previous work to support this claim.

claim: hth was downregulated in ph505-tumor cells.
source: Conversely, in our RNA-seq dataset hth was downregulated and at the protein level we confirmed that Hth is not ectopically expressed in the ph505 clones (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E–F).
evidence: The manuscript states this observation from RNA-seq and protein analysis with reference to figures.

claim: Hth is not ectopically expressed in ph505 clones.
source: Conversely, in our RNA-seq dataset hth was downregulated and at the protein level we confirmed that Hth is not ectopically expressed in the ph505 clones (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E–F).
evidence: The manuscript confirms this at protein level with reference to figures.

claim: ph505-tumors do not depend upon ectopic expression of Hth to keep cells in a non-differentiated state and support neoplastic growth.
source: Thus, our study reveals that ph505-tumors do not depend upon ectopic expression of Hth to keep cells in a non-differentiated state and support neoplastic growth.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion based on the lack of Hth expression.

claim: Even-skipped is ectopically expressed in ph505 clones.
source: We performed immunostaining for additional embryonic TFs, namely Even-skipped, Abdominal-B and Caudal, and observed ectopic expression of these proteins specifically in mutant clones (Figure 1D–E and Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–D).
evidence: The manuscript states this observation with reference to figures.

claim: Abdominal-B is ectopically expressed in ph505 clones.
source: We performed immunostaining for additional embryonic TFs, namely Even-skipped, Abdominal-B and Caudal, and observed ectopic expression of these proteins specifically in mutant clones (Figure 1D–E and Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–D).
evidence: The manuscript states this observation with reference to figures.

claim: Caudal is ectopically expressed in ph505 clones.
source: We performed immunostaining for additional embryonic TFs, namely Even-skipped, Abdominal-B and Caudal, and observed ectopic expression of these proteins specifically in mutant clones (Figure 1D–E and Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–D).
evidence: The manuscript states this observation with reference to figures.

claim: ph505-tumor cells previously committed to a neurogenesis-related path switch their cell fate as they fail to differentiate during tumorigenesis.
source: Overall, these results suggest that ph505-tumor cells previously committed to a neurogenesis-related path switch their cell fate as they fail to differentiate during the process of tumorigenesis due to the modulation of the transcriptional regulatory program of the cells.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this interpretation of the results.

claim: 24 transcription factors upregulated in ph505-tumor cells were selected for an in vivo screen.
source: Among all the TFs upregulated in ph505-tumor cells, we chose, based on literature search, 24 to assess their importance in promoting tumorigenic potential in these cells.
evidence: The manuscript describes the selection process for the screen.

claim: RNAi-mediated knock-down of cad, drm, kni, and bgcn in ph505 clones resulted in a strong increase in viability.
source: We compared effects of RNAi to the baseline ph505 neoplastic phenotype and observed that some RNAi lines targeting TFs (in ph505 clones) resulted in a strong increase in viability (close to 90–100%, for example cad, drm, kni, bgcn), while others did not change or only slightly changed pupal viability (Figure 2A).
evidence: The manuscript states this observation with reference to a figure.

claim: cad-KD in ph505 clones reduced tumor volume to 14%.
source: By quantifying tumor volumes relative to tissue size of the six above-mentioned perturbations, we observed that only cad-, drm-, kni- and bgcn-KD showed a significant difference compared to the baseline of 46% tumor volume in the ph505 condition (14, 13, 5 and 14% tumor volume, respectively).
evidence: The manuscript provides quantitative data on tumor volume reduction.

claim: drm-KD in ph505 clones reduced tumor volume to 13%.
source: By quantifying tumor volumes relative to tissue size of the six above-mentioned perturbations, we observed that only cad-, drm-, kni- and bgcn-KD showed a significant difference compared to the baseline of 46% tumor volume in the ph505 condition (14, 13, 5 and 14% tumor volume, respectively).
evidence: The manuscript provides quantitative data on tumor volume reduction.

claim: kni-KD in ph505 clones reduced tumor volume to 5%.
source: By quantifying tumor volumes relative to tissue size of the six above-mentioned perturbations, we observed that only cad-, drm-, kni- and bgcn-KD showed a significant difference compared to the baseline of 46% tumor volume in the ph505 condition (14, 13, 5 and 14% tumor volume, respectively).
evidence: The manuscript provides quantitative data on tumor volume reduction.

claim: bgcn-KD in ph505 clones reduced tumor volume to 14%.
source: By quantifying tumor volumes relative to tissue size of the six above-mentioned perturbations, we observed that only cad-, drm-, kni- and bgcn-KD showed a significant difference compared to the baseline of 46% tumor volume in the ph505 condition (14, 13, 5 and 14% tumor volume, respectively).
evidence: The manuscript provides quantitative data on tumor volume reduction.

claim: Higher eclosion rate is a good approximation for decreased tumor volume.
source: These results suggest that higher eclosion rate is a good approximation for decreased tumor volume.
evidence: The manuscript states this interpretation based on the correlation observed.

claim: kni-KD in ph505 clones showed the most striking decrease in tumor volume (9.2 fold decrease).
source: From all the RNAi conditions tested, kni-KD in ph505 mutant clones showed the most striking decrease in tumor volume (9.2 fold decrease), similar to the rescue experiment (ph505, UAS-ph) (Figure 2B).
evidence: The manuscript provides quantitative data with reference to a figure.

claim: The phenotype of adult eyes of ph505, kni-KD genotype suggests a recovery of the differentiation program.
source: Additionally, the phenotype of adult eyes of this genotype suggests a recovery of the differentiation program (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–D).
evidence: The manuscript states this observation with reference to figures.

claim: ELAV expression is no longer disrupted when expression of kni is blocked in ph505.
source: This is supported by immunostaining against ELAV showing that it is no longer disrupted when expression of kni is blocked in ph505 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: The manuscript states this observation with reference to a figure.

claim: The differentiation block observed in ph505-tumors is prevented upon reducing the level of knirps expression by RNAi KD.
source: Altogether, this shows that the differentiation block observed in ph505-tumors is prevented upon reducing the level of knirps expression by RNAi KD.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion based on ELAV expression data.

claim: A second, independent RNAi line against kni led to a significant decrease of tumor volume (14%) and an increase in eclosion rate (85%).
source: We confirmed that a second, independent RNAi line against kni also led to a significant decrease of tumor volume (14% of tumor volume vs. 46% in ph505) and an increase in eclosion rate (85%) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2F–J).
evidence: The manuscript provides quantitative data with reference to figures.

claim: The percentage of ph505-tumor-bearing hosts increased from 40% to 60% from the first week to subsequent weeks after transplantation.
source: In the case of the ph505-tumors the percentage of tumor-bearing hosts increased from 40% to 60%, from the first week to subsequent weeks after transplantation indicating hyperproliferation of the transplanted tissues (Figure 3A).
evidence: The manuscript provides quantitative data from transplantation assays with reference to a figure.

claim: The tumorigenic potential of ph505-transplanted tissue was detected on day seven after transplantation.
source: The tumorigenic potential of ph505-transplanted tissue was already detected on day seven after transplantation (Figure 3B).
evidence: The manuscript states this observation with reference to a figure.

claim: When transplanting ph505, kni-KD clones, no tumors were observed in the host flies within the first three weeks.
source: By contrast, when transplanting ph505, kni-KD clones we did not observe any tumors in the host flies within the first three weeks.
evidence: The manuscript states this observation from transplantation assays.

claim: After up to 5 weeks post-transplantation of ph505, kni-KD clones, only a single fly with GFP+ tissue overgrowth was found.
source: Even after up to 5 weeks post-transplantation, we could only find a single fly with GFP+ tissue overgrowth (Figure 3C–D).
evidence: The manuscript provides quantitative data from transplantation assays with reference to figures.

claim: Knirps plays a crucial role in tumorigenesis of ph505-tumors.
source: Our data demonstrate that the TF Knirps plays a crucial role in tumorigenesis of ph505-tumors given that kni-KD in these tissues not only led to a reduction of tumor volume but also the remaining clones were not able to proliferate in the host fly abdomen.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion based on transplantation and tumor volume data.

claim: Blocking apoptosis in ph505, kni-KD clones via expression of p35 was not sufficient to revert the anti-oncogenic effects of kni-KD.
source: However, we observed that blocking apoptosis in ph505, kni-KD clones was not sufficient to revert the anti-oncogenic effects of kni-KD (Figure 3G–H and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C–F).
evidence: The manuscript states this observation with reference to figures.

claim: The tumor volume of ph505, kni-KD, UAS-p35 was similar to ph505, kni-KD.
source: Furthermore, the tumor volume of ph505, kni-KD, UAS-p35 was similar to ph505, kni-KD (Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D–F).
evidence: The manuscript states this observation with reference to figures.

claim: FRT19A, kni-KD flies showed no difference in eclosion rate compared to control flies.
source: We also tested the effect of this particular RNAi line in the context of neutral clones generated with the same driver as for ph505-tumors. These FRT19A, kni-KD flies showed neither difference in eclosion rate nor in the adult eye phenotype, compared to control flies (Figure 3E–F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The manuscript states this observation with reference to figures.

claim: The RNAi line targeting kni does not per se affect eye-antennal imaginal disc development.
source: This suggests that the RNAi line targeting kni does not per se affect eye-antennal imaginal disc development.
evidence: The manuscript states this interpretation based on the lack of effect in control clones.

claim: Ectopic expression of kni in eye-antennal imaginal discs leads to the formation of cysts.
source: We thus assessed the effect of ectopic kni expression in eye-antennal imaginal discs by generating mitotic clones using again the eyFlp system. We observed that FRT19A clones expressing kni (Figure 4A) displayed a more pronounced round shape in comparison to the notchy-shape of FRT19A neutral clones (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A). Additionally, ectopic kni expression compromised the viability of the flies, evidenced by an eclosion rate of only 35% (Figure 4B), and the defective development of the adult eye structures (Figure 4C). Furthermore, we confirmed that ectopic expression of kni leads to the formation of cysts (Figure 4D) and thus interferes with epithelial polarity (Figure 4D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The manuscript states this observation with reference to figures.

claim: Ectopic kni expression compromised the viability of flies, with an eclosion rate of only 35%.
source: Additionally, ectopic kni expression compromised the viability of the flies, evidenced by an eclosion rate of only 35% (Figure 4B), and the defective development of the adult eye structures (Figure 4C).
evidence: The manuscript provides quantitative data with reference to a figure.

claim: Ectopic expression of kni interferes with epithelial polarity.
source: Furthermore, we confirmed that ectopic expression of kni leads to the formation of cysts (Figure 4D) and thus interferes with epithelial polarity (Figure 4D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The manuscript states this observation with reference to figures.

claim: Knirps is sufficient to generate tumors in host flies, visible 3 weeks after transplantation.
source: To test if ectopic expression of kni alone is sufficient to drive tumorigenesis we conducted transplantations of eye-antennal imaginal disc tissues ectopically expressing kni. We observed that knirps is sufficient to generate tumors in the host flies, visible 3 weeks after transplantation (ranging from 15–50%, from week 3 to 5 after transplantation respectively) (Figure 4E–F).
evidence: The manuscript provides quantitative data from transplantation assays with reference to figures.

claim: Ectopic expression of knirps interferes with the normal course of development.
source: Our data suggest that ectopic expression of knirps interferes with the normal course of development and that knirps is a new oncogene, possibly acting in a context/tissue-dependent manner.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion based on the data.

claim: Knirps is a new oncogene, possibly acting in a context/tissue-dependent manner.
source: Our data suggest that ectopic expression of knirps interferes with the normal course of development and that knirps is a new oncogene, possibly acting in a context/tissue-dependent manner.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion based on the data.

claim: JAK/STAT pathway was ectopically activated in knirps cyst-like clones.
source: We observed that of the JNK, JAK/STAT and Notch signaling pathways (all are activated in ph505-tumors [Classen et al., 2009; Martinez et al., 2009; Beira et al., 2018]), only JAK/STAT was ectopically activated, particularly in knirps cyst-like clones (Figure 5A–C).
evidence: The manuscript states this observation with citations and reference to figures.

claim: Ectopic expression of knirps alone is sufficient to activate the JAK/STAT pathway in mitotic clones.
source: This observation suggests that ectopic expression of knirps alone is sufficient to activate the JAK/STAT pathway in mitotic clones.
evidence: The manuscript states this interpretation based on the observation.

claim: Ectopic activation of JNK and Notch pathways in ph505-tumors is likely attributable to other factors regulated by Ph and independent of knirps.
source: Hence, ectopic activation of the other signaling pathways in ph505-tumors is likely attributable to other factors regulated by Ph and independent of knirps.
evidence: The manuscript states this interpretation based on the lack of JNK and Notch activation in kni-ectopic clones.

claim: ELAV expression was disrupted in kni-expressing cyst-like structures.
source: Similarly to what we observed with ph505 clones, ELAV expression was disrupted in kni-expressing cyst-like structures, as shown in Figure 5D, as well as Eya (Figure 5E), without ectopic activation of Hth (Figure 5F).
evidence: The manuscript states this observation with reference to figures.

claim: Eya expression was disrupted in kni-expressing cyst-like structures.
source: Similarly to what we observed with ph505 clones, ELAV expression was disrupted in kni-expressing cyst-like structures, as shown in Figure 5D, as well as Eya (Figure 5E), without ectopic activation of Hth (Figure 5F).
evidence: The manuscript states this observation with reference to figures.

claim: Hth was not ectopically activated in kni-expressing cyst-like structures.
source: Similarly to what we observed with ph505 clones, ELAV expression was disrupted in kni-expressing cyst-like structures, as shown in Figure 5D, as well as Eya (Figure 5E), without ectopic activation of Hth (Figure 5F).
evidence: The manuscript states this observation with reference to figures.

claim: Knirps alone is sufficient to initiate tumorigenesis.
source: These observations are thus in agreement with the hypothesis that knirps alone is sufficient to initiate tumorigenesis.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion based on the observations.

claim: JAK/STAT contributes to the differentiation block in ph505 and kni-ectopic tumors.
source: Our data argue in favor of a role for JAK/STAT in contributing to the differentiation block in ph505 and kni-ectopic tumors.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this interpretation.

claim: Upon blocking JAK/STAT in ph505-tumors, ELAV expression is re-established almost to a normal situation.
source: We decided to block this pathway in ph505-tumors (ph505, dome∆CYT) and examine cellular differentiation in these eye-antennal imaginal discs. Upon blocking JAK/STAT in ph505-tumors, we observed that ELAV expression is re-established almost to a normal situation, even in the presence of clones (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B in comparison to Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: The manuscript states this observation with reference to figures.

claim: The viability of ph505, dome∆CYT flies is increased, close to normal levels (eclosion rate 85%).
source: Moreover, the viability of these flies is increased, close to normal levels (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C, eclosion rate 85%) and some adult flies presented eye structures similar to wt individuals Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The manuscript provides quantitative data with reference to figures.

claim: Blockage of normal differentiation is a common feature between ph505 and kni-ectopic tumors in eye tissues.
source: Blockage of normal differentiation appears to be a common feature between ph505 and kni-ectopic tumors in eye tissues, suggesting that kni expression in the ph505-tumors contributes to the differentiation defects observed (Figure 1—figure supplement 3 and Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: The manuscript states this interpretation with reference to figures.

claim: Atonal (ato) was previously shown to have an anti-oncogenic role in the fly retina.
source: Atonal (ato), encoding a pro-neural TF, was previously shown to have an anti-oncogenic role in the fly retina, where it instructs tissue differentiation (Bossuyt et al., 2009).
evidence: The manuscript cites previous work to support this claim.

claim: ato is among the downregulated set of genes in ph505-tumors.
source: Notably, ato is also among our downregulated set of genes (padj. <0.01).
evidence: The manuscript states this observation from RNA-seq data.

claim: Ectopic expression of ato in ph505 clones led to a reduction of tumor volume from 46% to 3%.
source: We ectopically expressed ato in ph505 clones, which led to the rescue of the phenotype by a reduction of the tumor volume from 46% baseline to 3% and an increase in the eclosion rate from 12% to 84% (Figure 6A–C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–E).
evidence: The manuscript provides quantitative data with reference to figures.

claim: Ectopic expression of ato in ph505 clones led to an increase in eclosion rate from 12% to 84%.
source: We ectopically expressed ato in ph505 clones, which led to the rescue of the phenotype by a reduction of the tumor volume from 46% baseline to 3% and an increase in the eclosion rate from 12% to 84% (Figure 6A–C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–E).
evidence: The manuscript provides quantitative data with reference to figures.

claim: Expression of ato in ph505 clones was sufficient to restore the normal pattern of differentiation of eye-antennal tissue.
source: Hence, expression of ato in ph505 clones was sufficient to restore the normal pattern of differentiation of this tissue, as confirmed by the expression of ELAV (Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: The manuscript states this observation with reference to figures.

claim: There was an overall increase in proliferation levels in ph505-tumor tissues in comparison to control tissues.
source: Quantitative analysis showed an overall increase in proliferation levels in ph505-tumor tissues in comparison to control tissues.
evidence: The manuscript states this observation from quantitative analysis.

claim: The increase in proliferation in ph505-tumor tissues was largely due to an increase of proliferative cells outside of ph505 clones.
source: This was largely due to an increase of proliferative cells outside of ph505 clones (Figure 6—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: The manuscript states this observation with reference to a figure.

claim: There was a decrease in pH3+ cells inside clones co-expressing ph505 and atonal compared to ph505 clones.
source: The analysis also showed a decrease in pH3+ cells inside clones co-expressing ph505 and atonal (in comparison to ph505 clones) (Figure 6G).
evidence: The manuscript states this observation with reference to a figure.

claim: Atonal antagonizes ph tumor growth by counterbalancing proliferation.
source: Thus, atonal antagonizes ph tumor growth by counterbalancing proliferation, ultimately leading to a reduction of tumor burden and to a normal eye differentiation pattern.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this conclusion based on proliferation data.

claim: Tumor initiation is often linked to a loss of cellular identity.
source: Tumor initiation is often linked to a loss of cellular identity.
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Transcriptional programs determining cellular identity are preserved by epigenetically-acting chromatin factors.
source: Transcriptional programs determining cellular identity are preserved by epigenetically-acting chromatin factors.
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Epigenetic regulators are among the most frequently mutated genes in cancer.
source: Although such regulators are among the most frequently mutated genes in cancer, it is not well understood how an abnormal epigenetic condition contributes to tumor onset.
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: In larval tissue ph mutant cells show a shift towards an embryonic-like signature.
source: In larval tissue ph mutant cells show a shift towards an embryonic-like signature.
evidence: The manuscript states this finding in the abstract.

claim: The embryonic transcription factor knirps (kni) is a new oncogene.
source: Using loss- and gain-of-function experiments we uncovered the embryonic transcription factor knirps (kni) as a new oncogene.
evidence: The manuscript states this finding in the abstract.

claim: The oncogenic potential of kni lies in its ability to activate JAK/STAT signaling and block differentiation.
source: The oncogenic potential of kni lies in its ability to activate JAK/STAT signaling and block differentiation.
evidence: The manuscript states this finding in the abstract.

claim: Tumor growth in ph mutant cells can be substantially reduced by overexpressing a differentiation factor.
source: Conversely, tumor growth in ph mutant cells can be substantially reduced by overexpressing a differentiation factor.
evidence: The manuscript states this finding in the abstract.

claim: Epigenetically derailed tumor conditions can be reversed when targeting key players in the transcriptional network.
source: This demonstrates that epigenetically derailed tumor conditions can be reversed when targeting key players in the transcriptional network.
evidence: The manuscript states this conclusion in the abstract.

claim: Epigenetic regulators are responsible for controlling and restraining cellular plasticity during development.
source: During development, epigenetic regulators are responsible for controlling and restraining cellular plasticity.
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge with citations.

claim: An appropriate balance between proliferation and differentiation is fundamental.
source: An appropriate balance between proliferation and differentiation is fundamental and multiple regulatory layers of transcription factors and epigenetic regulators are employed to accomplish the underlying transcriptional control (Gonda and Ramsay, 2015; Piunti and Shilatifard, 2016).
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Many epigenetic regulators are evolutionary conserved.
source: Many epigenetic regulators are evolutionary conserved and among the most commonly mutated genes in human cancer (Piunti and Shilatifard, 2016).
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge with citation.

claim: Disruption of epigenetic constraints leads to global reorganization of the epigenome and changes in transcriptional profiles.
source: Disruption of epigenetic constraints leads to global reorganization of the epigenome and changes in transcriptional profiles, which might provide a cellular state permissive for tumorigenesis (Wainwright and Scaffidi, 2017).
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge with citation.

claim: Transcription factors are less prone to be bypassed by alternative mutational events compared to signaling pathways.
source: Transcription factors (TFs) are less prone to be bypassed by alternative mutational events, and their perturbation can affect several cancer hallmarks.
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge with citation.

claim: PcG proteins are organized into two basic complexes, PRC1 and PRC2.
source: PcG proteins are organized into two basic complexes, Polycomb repressive complex 1 and 2 (PRC1 and PRC2) (Piunti and Shilatifard, 2016).
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge with citation.

claim: Homeotic genes encoding Homeobox TFs are classical PcG targets.
source: One example of classical PcG targets are homeotic genes encoding Homeobox TFs, first identified in Drosophila and responsible for correct spatial body development in flies (Shah and Sukumar, 2010; Abate-Shen, 2002).
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge with citations.

claim: The altered expression of Hox genes in human tumors suggests important roles for both oncogenesis and tumor suppression.
source: The altered expression of Hox genes in human tumors suggests important roles for both oncogenesis and tumor suppression (Shah and Sukumar, 2010), which further hints towards an role for PcG proteins in oncogenesis.
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge with citation.

claim: The tumor suppressive role of PcG proteins in Drosophila imaginal discs has been extensively investigated.
source: The tumor suppressive role of PcG proteins, in particular PRC1 members in Drosophila imaginal discs, has been extensively investigated (Classen et al., 2009; Martinez et al., 2009).
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge with citations.

claim: kni is a gap gene involved in the subdivision of the embryo anterior-posterior axis.
source: kni is a gap gene involved in the subdivision of the embryo anterior-posterior axis that can function as an activator (Langeland et al., 1994) or a repressor (Pankratz et al., 1990).
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge with citations.

claim: kni is required for vein formation in wing imaginal discs.
source: Besides its classic function in embryonic development, kni is subsequently also required for vein formation in wing imaginal discs (Lunde et al., 2003).
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge with citation.

claim: Misexpression of TFs in imaginal discs and formation of cysts has been suggested to be an indicator of precancerous lesions.
source: Misexpression of TFs in imaginal discs and formation of cysts has been suggested to be an indicator of precancerous lesions (Bielmeier et al., 2016).
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge with citation.

claim: Loss of differentiation capabilities and the emergence of a progenitor-like state are common processes observed in cancer.
source: Loss of differentiation capabilities, as well as the emergence of a progenitor-like state that promotes cellular transformation and tumor initiation are common processes observed in cancer (Roy and Hebrok, 2015; Bossuyt et al., 2009).
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Neurons lacking the TF Lola dedifferentiate, turn on neural stem cell genes, begin to divide, and form tumors in Drosophila.
source: The concept of dedifferentiation preceding tumorigenesis has been shown in Drosophila neurons, where neurons lacking the TF Lola dedifferentiate, turning on neural stem cell genes, begin to divide, and form tumors (Southall et al., 2014).
evidence: The manuscript cites this as an example with citation.

claim: Hyperactivation of the JAK/STAT pathway has been observed in different human cancers.
source: Hyperactivation of the JAK/STAT pathway has been observed in different human cancers, where it activates survival and proliferation genes (Buchert et al., 2016).
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge with citation.

claim: JAK/STAT pathway activation maintains cells in a less differentiated and more proliferative state.
source: Also, cells can be maintained in a less differentiated and more proliferative state by JAK/STAT pathway activation, as highlighted by its activation in stem cell niches in Drosophila (Hou et al., 2002; Amoyel and Bach, 2012; Christofi and Apidianakis, 2013) and in mouse embryonic stem cells (Hao et al., 2006).
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge with citations.

claim: The JAK/STAT pathway must be switched off to allow differentiation of hematopoietic progenitors in flies.
source: Furthermore, there is evidence suggesting that this pathway must be switched off to allow differentiation of hematopoietic progenitors in flies (Amoyel and Bach, 2012).
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge with citation.

claim: Blocking JAK/STAT activity suppresses the PRC1 mutant tumor phenotype.
source: In agreement with this, blocking JAK/STAT activity suppresses the PRC1 mutant tumor phenotype (Classen et al., 2009) and in our hands induces the re-establishment of the differentiation program characteristic of eye-antennal imaginal discs.
evidence: The manuscript cites previous work and states their own observation.

claim: Using the blockage of signaling pathways as a therapeutic target has been shown to be difficult due to the redundancy of the signaling networks.
source: However, using the blockage of signaling pathways as a therapeutic target has been shown to be difficult due to the redundancy of the signaling networks and thus acquired drug resistance is common in cancer cells (Gonda and Ramsay, 2015; Buchert et al., 2016).
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Differentiation therapy has led to favorable outcomes in acute myeloid leukemia.
source: The significance of these observations, referred to as 'differentiation therapy', is supported by work done in acute myeloid leukemia where therapies to overcome the cellular differentiation arrest have led to favorable outcomes (Gocek and Marcinkowska, 2011).
evidence: The manuscript cites this as supporting evidence with citation.

claim: Differentiation therapy has been suggested to restrict the cellular plasticity of cancer stem cells.
source: Moreover this strategy has also been suggested to restrict the cellular plasticity of cancer stem cells (Wainwright and Scaffidi, 2017).
evidence: The manuscript cites this as supporting evidence with citation.

claim: caudal, grain and knirps were predicted as TFs putatively responsible for all differentially expressed genes in the RNA-seq dataset.
source: Employing the iRegulon tool (Janky et al., 2014), predictions based on motif enrichment revealed caudal, grain and knirps (direct Ph targets in eye discs [Loubière et al., 2016]) as TFs putatively responsible for all differentially expressed genes in our RNA-seq dataset.
evidence: The manuscript states this finding from computational analysis with citations.

claim: caudal, grain and knirps are direct Ph targets in eye discs.
source: Employing the iRegulon tool (Janky et al., 2014), predictions based on motif enrichment revealed caudal, grain and knirps (direct Ph targets in eye discs [Loubière et al., 2016]) as TFs putatively responsible for all differentially expressed genes in our RNA-seq dataset.
evidence: The manuscript cites this as established knowledge with citation.

claim: An image analysis pipeline was developed to measure the volume of mutant clones and tissue volume.
source: To better quantify changes of tumor volume in these tissues we developed an image analysis pipeline (see Materials and methods). This enabled us to concomitantly measure the volume of mutant clones (GFP-labeled) as well as the volume of the tissue.
evidence: The manuscript describes the development of this method.

claim: The sequencing data is available under GEO accession number GSE101463.
source: The accession number for the sequencing data reported in this paper is GEO: GSE101463.
evidence: The manuscript provides the data availability information.
